findings.detail: The new per-interface gate uses accepted fully-failed cohesive quadrature reference area (D exactly 1), validates fraction=area/activated-reference-area and cross-run activation-area agreement at 1e-6 relative, then applies the 0.02 absolute fraction-difference limit. It counts closed failed faces as constitutively debonded while keeping geometric opening separate.

The stage capacity triplet requires each adjacent pair damage/debond gate. Enabled paper damage remains inconclusive because the per-tet damage index is not mesh-objective crack area; geometric crack/open-debond area remains separately unavailable. Matching force alone cannot pass.
A role is not_enabled only when both histories report not_enabled; mixed enablement or incompatible reference area is inconclusive/fails closed.

Tests cover a below-limit 1.9 percentage-point constitutive-debond difference, an above-limit 2.1-point difference, force-match with enabled-but-unmeasured paper damage, legacy face-maximum status, and mismatched activated area.

limitations: This is a source/analyzer review and Python unit test only; it is not native or physical qualification.
The accepted constitutive capacity-loss area is not geometric open area.
